liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (3 reviews): Reviewer's first He's Gone and Spoonful after Brent's death; played passionately, moving the listener to tears while standing; Second-set He's Gone into Spoonful, Jam and Drums was the standout stretch of the night [12][13][21]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 other source): Setlist shows China Cat Sunflower flowing into I Know You Rider, and He's Gone into Spoonful and Jam [1]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Described as sweet in the second set, before a perfect He's Gone into Spoonful and a strong jam [19]
- **Spoonful** (1 other source): A healthy jam emerges out of Spoonful [10]

## The recordings

- **gd90-09-11.sbd-matrix.wiley.11809.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 166 min; rated 3.47/5 by 19 [1]. Said about its sound: Healy mix likely beats the Spectrum's house sound, but China Cat and Rider come from an audience recording, not soundboard [13]
- **gd90-09-11.fob-nak300.wiley.11808.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 167 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has exceptional sound quality for an AUD source [21]
- **gd1990-09-11.146063.FOB.BK4011.Brotman.Metchick.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 21 songs; 179 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [10]
- **gd1990-09-11.AKG451.Currier.Keo.121665.Flac1644**: audience recording; 23 songs; 179 min [3]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls the show vividly, standing still and emotional rather than dancing, missing Brent [12]
- Attendee sat sixth row on Jerry's side, first time up close to the band's new lineup [13]
- Vince's fourth show on the road; electric parking-lot mood suggested a memorable Spectrum night, and two openers hinted the same [14]
- Brent had just died and it was Vince's fourth show; the attendee found it eerie and felt the band might be ending [17]
- Attendee found the parking lot a disaster, full of young people getting wasted, and felt Vince was picked too quickly [18]
- Reviewer says Jerry played with fire, and the first set was tight yet loose-sounding [19]
- Attendee began near Phil, who was slapping the bass hard early, then moved to the back of the floor [21]
- Attendee had driven a school bus across the states, blew the engine in New Mexico, and rejoined the tour here; recalls snow [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-09-11.sbd-matrix.wiley.11809.sbeok.shnf**: source: (Healy Mix)SBD>DAT>C>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN [1]
- **gd90-09-11.fob-nak300.wiley.11808.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB(Nak. 300's>D-5)>CM>?>CDR>WAV>SHN [2]
- **gd1990-09-11.146063.FOB.BK4011.Brotman.Metchick.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Dave Brotman & Jeff Metchick Master Digital Recording; transferred by Charlie Miller Transfer Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel; source: Recording info: B&K 4011 (110°) > B&K power supply > Master DAT (Panasonic SV-250/48k). Location: FOB; Sec, 102 Row 14, Seat 13 (mics on stand @ 6') [10]
- **gd1990-09-11.AKG451.Currier.Keo.121665.Flac1644**: taped by Mr. Currier; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By MR. Currier, Transfer By Keo; AKGC451EB/CK1's>AKG 9V Phantom Power>Marantz PDM 430> Probaly Dolby (Not Marked)>Tapes Maxell… [3]
